identity.title: A Taxonomy of Challenges to Curating Fair Datasets

problem.claim: Understand and improve the practical curation of fair machine-learning datasets.

gap.claim: Practical aspects of fair-dataset curation remain insufficiently understood despite extensive efforts to create fairer datasets.

contributions.claim: A taxonomy of challenges and trade-offs encountered across the dataset-curation lifecycle, derived from interviews with 30 ML dataset curators.
Recommendations intended to foster systemic changes that better facilitate fair-dataset curation practices.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a comprehensive lifecycle-oriented taxonomy grounded in interviews with 30 dataset curators.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report findings that reveal overarching issues in the broader fairness landscape affecting data curation.

narrative_sequence.summary: Fairer datasets have received extensive effort, but practical curation remains poorly understood.
Interviews with 30 ML dataset curators support a taxonomy of lifecycle challenges and trade-offs.
The reported findings identify broader fairness issues affecting curation and motivate recommendations for systemic change.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a practical knowledge gap to an interview-based taxonomy spanning the full curation lifecycle, then to systemic recommendations.

lessons.interpretation: A useful research narrative can align the scope of the empirical inquiry with the scope of the proposed intervention.
lessons.application: For a socio-technical problem, define the lifecycle or process studied, organize observed tensions across that scope, and derive recommendations at the corresponding systemic level.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the work targets a narrowly bounded mechanism or has evidence from only one stage of a process.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the taxonomy’s categories, the concrete trade-offs or broader fairness issues identified, or the recommendations’ details.
It does not report interview selection, analysis procedures, participant distribution, or any evaluation of the recommendations.
